title: private-deploy-networking-incident-notes
content:
Summary:
- Notes and breadcrumbs for the networking incident affecting private deployments in eu-west-1 (customers A & B).
- Symptoms: inter-VPC traffic intermittently failing, TLS handshakes sometimes succeed but app-level connections time out, DNS resolving to correct private IPs but connection resets.

Timeline (local times):
- 2026-02-24 08:10: customer reported 503s and connection timeouts to private endpoint (redwood-private.example).
- 2026-02-24 09:05 triage call, confirmed issue reproducible from internal jump-host in customer VPC.
- 2026-02-24 09:20 started collecting logs, packet captures, route table dumps.

Hypotheses (short):
- VPC peering route/tgw propagation issue (routes not propagated or conflicting).
- Security group / NACL intermittently blocking return path (egress vs ingress mismatch).
- Split-horizon private DNS misconfigured - SVC resolves to wrong AZ/VPC sometimes.
- NAT gateway / egress path overloaded causing connection resets/timeouts.
- TLS: SNI or intermediate firewall doing TLS inspection and resetting session for large payloads.
- MTU/path MTU causing fragmentation and resets on certain paths.

Commands tried / outputs (partial):
1) DNS resolution checks (from customer app host):
- dig +short redwood-private.example @10.0.0.2 -> 10.10.32.45
- dig +trace redwood-private.example shows private zone authoritative in us-east internal-hosted-zone; weird that query forwarded to us-east from eu-west resolver sometimes
- nslookup redwood-private.example 169.254.169.253 -> NXDOMAIN occasionally (observed at 2026-02-24T08:58)

Notes: split-horizon/route53 private zone alignment mismatch suspected. Maya saw zone association list incorrectly including a dev VPC.

2) Connectivity and TCP tests (from jump host in customer VPC):
- curl -v --connect-timeout 10 https://redwood-private.example/health -> sometimes 200, often hangs then: "curl: (28) Operation timed out after 10001 milliseconds"
- openssl s_client -connect 10.10.32.45:443 -servername redwood-private.example
  -> sometimes full cert chain, sometimes TLS handshake fails: "140735206144816:error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:sslv3 alert handshake failure"
- telnet 10.10.32.45 443 -> "Connected" then immediate close in some attempts
- nc -v -w 5 10.10.32.45 443 -> "Connection timed out" or "Connection refused" depending on attempt

3) ICMP / path checks:
- ping -c 5 10.10.32.45 -> replies stable when successful, but 30% packet loss observed in failing window.
- traceroute -n 10.10.32.45 -> path includes TGW hops (10.100.x.x) then disappears; one hop shows flapping ASN 64512 (suspect transit config)

4) Route table / peering checks (AWS console + awscli):
- aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-0a12... -> routes showed route to peering-abc with target pcx-0f...
- aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections --filters Name=status-code,Values=active -> pcx-0f active but last-accepted timestamp older than change window
- Observed duplicate routes (overlapping CIDRs 10.10.0.0/16 vs 10.10.32.0/20) - potential route preference instability

5) Security groups / NACLs:
- Checked SGs: allowed 443 from customer CIDR and redwood infra CIDR.
- NACLs on subnet: stateless; logs showed DENY entries for ephemeral ports in a few windows (possible manual rule change by infra team earlier)

6) Packet capture (tcpdump) on redwood side ENI:
- Observed SYN from client, SYN-ACK from server, then RST from an intermediate IP (10.100.1.2) within TGW; sometimes no RST and connection established.
- Some packets show DF set and Ethernet frame size ~1500, suggesting fragmentation not happening.

7) MTU check:
- ping -s 1400 -M do 10.10.32.45 -> fragmentation required / unreachable in some hops.
- Reduced PMTU to 1300 in tests, improved stability for short-lived connections.

Immediate remediation steps tried:
- Added explicit routes in customer route table to target pcx-0f for 10.10.32.0/20 (workaround for overlapping CIDR) -> reduced errors by ~40% for 1 hour.
- Temporarily opened more permissive NACL rules to allow all ephemeral ports (40000-65535) -> improved return path success.
- Re-associated correct Route53 private zone with eu-west VPC (rollback of earlier dev change) -> seemed to remove NXDOMAINs.

Longer-term action items / TODOs:
- (INF-4821) Confirm TGW propagation state and remove conflicting route advertisements. Owner: Samir. Due: 2026-03-05.
- Verify NACL change history across affected subnets and implement guardrails to prevent accidental DENY rule insertion. Owner: SRE.
- Add health-check and telemetry on TLS handshake success rates per AZ (Console dashboard). Owner: Observability.
- Investigate MTU across TGW path - consider enabling TCP MSS clamping on edge or adjusting ENI MTU. Owner: Infra.
- Add end-to-end synthetic tests from each customer VPC to private endpoint (runbook + scheduled). Owner: Solutions Eng.

Notes / lessons learned:
- Overlapping CIDR blocks between teams (dev vs prod) caused intermittent route selection issues; explicit host prefixes helped but need policy enforcement.
- Split-horizon DNS changes are high-risk; require change windows and quick rollback plan.
- Small MTU/fragmentation issues can manifest as TLS failures; include MTU checks in baseline network tests.

Next debugging commands to run (if it reoccurs):
- tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/conn.pcap host 10.10.32.45 and collect on both customer hop and redwood ENI simultaneously.
- mtr -r -c 100 10.10.32.45 (to get latency/loss over time).
- curl --resolve redwood-private.example:443:10.10.32.45 -v --trace-ascii /tmp/curl.trace https://redwood-private.example/health
- openssl s_client -connect 10.10.32.45:443 -servername redwood-private.example -msg -debug
- aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-attachments --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0abcd... - check route propagation state

Random notes to self:
- Talk to network team about flapping ASN in traceroute (64512). Could be on-prem partner or misconfigured VPN.
- Keep a copy of the relaxed NACL rule change (audit record) for postmortem.
- We should add a synthetic that repeatedly performs TLS handshake + POST of ~8kb payload to catch MTU issues.

Slack breadcrumbs:
- @maya saw dev VPC mistakenly associated with private zone at 08:45 -> reverted at 09:12.
- @samir applied temporary route change at 10:03 -> noted improvement.

End of notes.

(Will convert to postmortem outline after root cause confirmed.)
